_comment: Terminal geometry, per airport, from OpenStreetMap via Overpass.
aliases FIX WHAT terminal_key CANNOT KNOW. That function reads a name and
resolves 'Heathrow Terminal 5', 'T2 (International)' and 'T5, Pier F' on its
own. What it deliberately refuses to guess is which TERMINAL a pier or a
concourse belongs to -- 'Pier 6' is not Terminal 6 and 'Flugsteig G' is not
Terminal G -- because that is an airport-specific fact. Those live here.
EVERY ALIAS BELOW WAS CHECKED GEOGRAPHICALLY, not assumed. FRA's Flugsteig
G, H and J sit within 740m of each other and 1.7-2.0km from Terminal 1, so
they are their own building -- Terminal 3, which is what FRA's dining rows
call it. LHR's 'T3IB' is 506m from 'Terminal 3, Pier 6' and further from
everything else.
exclude DROPS BUILDINGS THAT ARE NOT A TERMINAL YOU CAN STAND IN AND EAT IN.
General aviation terminals, private suites, a railway station and a first
class lounge are all tagged aeroway=terminal in OSM and none of them belongs
on a departures-board schematic. 'New Terminal 1' at JFK is under
construction, has no gates, and overlaps the existing Terminal 1 -- drawn, it
is a ghost building on top of a real one.
expect_terminals AND min_gates ARE THE TRIPWIRE. If OSM is edited and a
terminal disappears or its gates are retagged, the run is REFUSED and the
previous map is kept. A quiet empty map is worse than no map.
KNOWN GAPS, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER:
EWR  OSM has only Terminal A as a named passenger terminal. B and C are
absent, so two thirds of Newark cannot be drawn at all.
LGA  Terminal C is absent from OSM. Terminal B is present as its Eastern
and Western Concourses.
HKG  Terminal 2 genuinely has no gates -- it is check-in and ground
transport only -- so a zero there is correct, not a fetch failure.
FRA, LHR, EWR  have terminal geometry but NO dining coordinates and no
gate hints, so their maps can show the building and the gates and no
food at all. The screen has to say so.
